items.title: TTGBench: Benchmarking Topological Evolution and Semantic Drift in Text-attributed Temporal Graphs
items.abstract: Temporal graph learning models the evolution of dynamic systems, where both structural interactions and semantic states change over time. However, existing benchmarks primarily emphasize structural evolution via temporal link prediction (TLP), while support for semantic evolution remains limited. Although temporal node classification (TNC) is sometimes included, it is typically restricted to simplistic binary settings that fail to capture realistic semantic drift. Moreover, commonly used datasets exhibit high link repetition, leading to inflated performance estimates and obscuring true model capability. To address these limitations, we introduce \textbf{TTGBench}, a new benchmark that jointly evaluates structural and semantic evolution. TTGBench comprises six real-world, text-rich datasets characterized by \emph{Dual Volatility}, enabling rigorous and fair evaluation of existing models. Notably, it is the first benchmark to support both multi-class and multi-label TNC, filling a critical gap in evaluating temporal semantic drift. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of 17 state-of-the-art methods across Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs) and Large Language Model (LLM)-based paradigms. The results reveal a clear \emph{capability divide} between the two paradigms: TGNN-based methods excel at structural prediction but fail at semantic tracking, whereas LLM-based predictors show the opposite trend. Through in-depth analysis, we uncover their fundamental limitations and provide insights for developing more comprehensive temporal graph models.

items.title: Türkiye century maarif model: English language teachers' adaptation to changing educational technologies and future perceptions
items.abstract: The purpose of this exploratory qualitative case study is to examine adaptation to changing educational technologies in English language teaching and teachers’ perceptions of the future within the framework of the Türkiye Century Maarif Model (TCMM), which emphasizes a learnercentered, holistic approach to pedagogical technology integration. In this context, the research addresses how teachers adopt technology in the classroom environment and associate their perceptions regarding the future with this model. The study group consists of four EFL teachers (pre-service teachers in the practicum process and inservice teachers working under the Ministry of National Education [MoNE] in Türkiye) selected through purposive convenience sampling. Research data were collected through a semi-structured, scenario-based open-ended qualitative questionnaire and analyzed systematically using Corbin and Strauss’s (2008) coding framework. The findings reveal both individual perceptions regarding the use of technology in English teaching and practice-based insights within the framework of the TCMM. The analysis indicated that English language teachers demonstrated pedagogical resilience through peer learning and a subordinate strategy, despite facing various systemic barriers. Moreover, participants perceived artificial intelligence (AI) in EFL education as a supportive tool and a “critical friend” rather than a replacement for educators. Ultimately, this study provides initial exploratory insights that contribute to the ongoing discourse on technological adaptation under emerging national curriculum frameworks.

items.title: Vision: Data-Centric Anchoring for Robust and Interpretable Agentic AI
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems built on large language models fail in two persistent ways that scaling does not fix: they break under distribution shift, and they cannot explain the decisions they make. We argue these are co-symptoms of one structural deficiency in the data lifecycle that governs how agents are trained, evaluated, and deployed. Observational interaction logs record what an agent did, not what it would have done otherwise. They encode spurious correlations without controlled variation, so they lack the counterfactual structure needed to separate causal signal from coincidence or to validate an explanation. No model-centric method can recover invariances the data never contained. We present Data-Centric Anchoring: robustness and interpretability should be engineered into the data environment, not extracted from models after training. Our central contribution is the Data-Centric Agentic Loop, a four-stage framework of Curate, Augment, Constrain, and Attribute. The ordering is structural, not stylistic. Curation precedes augmentation because generative models amplify whatever bias they are trained on. Augmentation precedes constraint because invariance objectives are vacuous without variation across environments to be invariant to. Attribution closes the loop, converting observed failures into targeted data interventions for the next iteration. Each stage manufactures the preconditions of the next, which makes the loop self-correcting rather than merely sequential. We ground the framework in a failure-driven taxonomy that links four core failure modes to the data lifecycle: spurious feature reliance, distribution-shift fragility, uncertainty miscalibration, and explanation unfaithfulness. We close with the limits of this approach and the open problems that stand between it and practical deployment at scale.

items.title: We Advocate for Interpretive Depth: Confronting Methodological Drift and Reclaiming the Researcher's Soul in AI-Integrated Qualitative Inquiry
items.abstract: Nguyen, T.H.A., Nguyen-Trung, K. (2026, September 7-9). We Advocate for Interpretive Depth: Confronting Methodological Drift and Reclaiming the Researcher’s Soul in AI-Integrated Qualitative Inquiry. [Conference presentation]. The 2nd Global Qualitative Research Conference, Cebu City, Philippines. Abstract We invite the qualitative research community to confront the rapid, often uncritical adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence in qualitative data analysis. Based on our comprehensive review of 192 scholarly publications from 2022 to 2025, we observe a concerning and frequently unintentional drift toward post-positivist "small q" logics. Even when researchers claim to follow reflexive "Big Q" frameworks, we find that the reliance on statistical validation and inter-coder agreement often displaces the interpretive depth essential to our craft. We highlight critical lessons learned, focusing on the systemic shift toward descriptive topic summaries that strip the "soul" from participant narratives and the persistent lack of transparency in technical workflows. In this presentation, we cover the methodology strands of Ethics, Trustworthiness, and Data Analysis, specifically addressing the problematic maneuvers of "inherited legitimacy" and "normative silence" used to bypass ethical oversight. We contribute to the field’s best practices by providing a strategic roadmap for reclaiming the human researcher as the absolute ontological anchor of inquiry. We advocate for iterative "wordsmithing" in prompt engineering and the establishment of radical transparency through technical audit trails and multi-model triangulation. Ultimately, we argue that technological efficiency must never compromise the methodological congruence or the ethical integrity of the human-centered research tradition. Keywords Generative Artificial Intelligence Qualitative Data Analysis Qualitative Research Methodology Reflexivity Research Ethics Methodological Congruence Bios Thi-Hong-Anh Nguyen is an independent researcher with interests in digitalization, qualitative methodology, and organizational analysis. Drawing on experience in research on AI-integrated HR technologies, her work examines the use of generative AI in human resource management and qualitative data analysis, with a broader interest in how emerging technologies shape organizations and research practice. Kien Nguyen-Trung is GEDSI & Research Lead at Water Sensitive Cities Australia, Monash University. An applied qualitative sociologist, he works at the intersection of disaster risk, climate adaptation, socio-behavioural change, and qualitative research innovation. He serves as Editor at The Qualitative Report and on the editorial board of the International Journal of Qualitative Methods, and co-edited a book (2026) Critical Disaster Studies in Asia and the Pacific.
